# System and capability

Candidate definition for our scope: a **system** is a bounded arrangement of interacting elements considered together in relation to an intended purpose. This is a proposed operational convention, not a claim that every natural or conceptual system necessarily has a human purpose.

People, processes, information and tools are common elements, not four mandatory ingredients of every system. The earlier restrictive ingredient list is superseded as a proposal by this broader candidate. Boundaries, relevant environment, dependencies, configuration and interactions need explicit treatment.

A **capability** provisionally means an ability of an arrangement to produce a specified effect under specified conditions. Possessing a capability, performing it successfully on one occasion, sustaining it over time, and helping meet an underlying need are different claims.

Example: topic discovery, retained source references and human selection can form an arrangement intended to support writing. An external office handoff may be essential even if excluded from the boundary chosen for Dream. A scheduler or tool alone does not establish this whole arrangement's usefulness.

## Implementation and operation

Candidate definition: an **implementation** is a concrete realization of a design or description. An implementation can be incomplete or defective; its completeness, readiness and effectiveness are assessed separately. **Implementing** names the activity of producing that realization. **Operation** is the actual functioning or use of an arrangement.

For example, a transfer routine with no retry handling is still an implementation; whether it is usable or meets its requirements under network failure requires a separate assessment. A design document alone is not the operating implementation it describes. The [NASA source account](../../../../source-locators.md#source-523d0cb6d1fd537e) informs this separation. These meanings do not introduce implementation instructions or verification methods into this standard.

See [composition](../../mereology/composition-and-boundaries.md), [execution](../../execution/behavior-and-responsibility.md), [assessment](../../assessment/requirement-and-need-fulfillment.md), and [SEBoK source account](../../../../source-locators.md#source-1c0e5ffee91d5762).
